en.title: DreamWorks Animation Returns to '90s Filipino Glory with Forgotten Island
en.summary: DreamWorks Animation is set to recapture the magic of its '90s heyday with an original fantasy-comedy. "Forgotten Island" promises a vibrant story of friendship set against a unique cultural backdrop.
en.body:
DreamWorks Animation, a studio that has gifted us with unforgettable characters and worlds since 1998, is gearing up for a triumphant return to its '90s glory days with a brand-new original film, **Forgotten Island**. This upcoming fantasy-comedy is poised to transport audiences to the 1990s Philippines, introducing us to two soon-to-be inseparable best friends, Jo and Raissa. Voiced by the talented H.E.R. and Liza Soberano respectively, their journey into a magical realm could be the very thing that tests the strength of their budding friendship.

The creative engine behind **Forgotten Island** is the writing-directing team of **Joel Crawford** and **Januel Mercado**, whose own two-decade-long friendship has clearly informed the film's core themes. "For two decades, we have put so much of ourselves into every movie we do together," Crawford shares. "That can be just jokes, things that make us laugh, or themes about being in the moment that we both really value in our own lives." Their collaboration began as story artists on **Kung Fu Panda 2**, and after working on successful sequels like **The Croods: A New Age** and the Oscar-nominated **Puss in Boots: The Last Wish**, they were eager to embark on an entirely original project.

"We wanted to do something original, but really original in every sense of the word," Crawford explains. "So building a story around friendship, and our friendship, seemed the best place to start." This focus on authentic connection is mirrored in the on-screen dynamic between Jo, described as a livewire, and Raissa, a smartypants, whose contrasting personalities are sure to create sparks and generate plenty of laughs.

## A New World of Adventure

The choice to set **Forgotten Island** in the 1990s Philippines offers a rich tapestry of cultural detail and a distinct visual identity that sets it apart from many previous DreamWorks offerings. This era, often fondly remembered for its unique blend of emerging technology and enduring traditions, provides a fertile ground for a story about friendship and discovery. The film's premise, where a magical quest might jeopardize the very bond that drives it, promises a narrative with genuine emotional stakes, appealing to both longtime fans of the studio's character-driven epics and newcomers alike.

## The Heart of Friendship

For the dedicated WeCult audience, **Forgotten Island** represents more than just another animated feature; it signifies DreamWorks Animation's commitment to original storytelling and its ability to tap into universal themes through diverse cultural lenses. The emphasis on a deeply personal friendship, born from the real-life bond of its creators, suggests an authenticity that resonates with fans who have grown up with characters like Shrek and Hiccup. The anticipation builds around how Jo and Raissa's adventure will explore the complexities of connection, offering a relatable narrative that celebrates the power of true friendship, a concept that has long been the secret sauce of DreamWorks's most beloved films.

## What's Next

While specific release dates for **Forgotten Island** have not yet been announced, the project's development signifies an exciting new chapter for DreamWorks Animation. Fans can look forward to further details regarding the film's visual style, supporting cast, and the magical elements that will define Jo and Raissa's unforgettable journey.

tr.title: DreamWorks Animation '90'lı Yılların Filipin Hazinesini Unutulmuş Ada ile Geri Dönüyor
tr.summary: DreamWorks Animation, unutulmaz karakterler ve dünyalar sunan stüdyo, yeni bir orijinal film olan 'Unutulmuş Ada' ile '90'lı yılların Filipin altın çağını geri getirmeye hazırlanıyor. Bu yeni fantezi-komedi, izleyicileri 1990'lı yıllar Filipinlerine götürecek ve iki yeni dost Jo ve Raissa'nın hikayesini anlatıyor.
tr.body:
DreamWorks Animation, 1998'den beri unutulmaz karakterler ve dünyalar sunan bir stüdyo, yeni bir orijinal film olan **Unutulmuş Ada** ile '90'lı yılların altın çağına geri dönüyor. Bu yeni fantezi-komedi, izleyicileri 1990'lı yıllar Filipinlerine götürecek ve iki yeni dost Jo ve Raissa'nın hikayesini anlatıyor. H.E.R. ve Liza Soberano tarafından seslendirilen bu iki karakter, bir büyülü realmde karşılaşıyor ve bu karşılaşma onların dostluğunu sınayacak. 

 ## Yeni Bir Macera Dünyası 

 **Unutulmuş Ada**'nın yaratıcı ekibi, yazar-yönetmen ikilisi **Joel Crawford** ve **Januel Mercado**, kendi iki thập yıllık dostluğunu filmde yansıtıyor. Crawford, 'İki thập yıl boyunca, birlikte yaptığımız her filme kendimizden bir şeyler katıyoruz' diyor. 'Bu, sadece komik şeyler, bizi güldüren şeyler veya hayatımızda gerçekten önemli gördüğümüz anların teması olabilir.' Crawford ve Mercado, **Kung Fu Panda 2**'de hikaye sanatçıları olarak birlikte çalışmaya başladılar ve **The Croods: A New Age** ve Oscar'a aday gösterilen **Puss in Boots: The Last Wish** gibi başarılı devam filmlerinde çalıştıktan sonra, tamamen orijinal bir proje üzerinde çalışmaya karar verdi. 

 Crawford, 'Tamamen orijinal bir şey yapmak istedik, gerçekten her anlamda orijinal' diyor. 'Bu nedenle, hikayeyi dostluk ve bizim dostluğumuz حولunda inşa etmek en iyi yer gibi görünüyordu.' Bu, Jo ve Raissa arasındaki ekran kimyasında da görülüyor. Jo, bir 'canlı elektrik' olarak tanımlanıyor, Raissa ise 'zeka' olarak tanımlanıyor ve onların zıt kişilikleri arasında yaşanacak çatışmalar ve komik anlar olacak. 

 ## Dostluğun Kalbi 

 **Unutulmuş Ada**, DreamWorks Animation'ın orijinal hikaye anlatımına ve evrensel temaları çeşitli kültürel lenslerle yakalama能力ine bağlılığını temsil ediyor. Yaratıcılarının gerçek dostluğundan doğan bu film, Shrek ve Hiccup gibi karakterlerle büyüyen WeCult okuyucuları için önemli bir anlam taşıyor. Jo ve Raissa'nın macerasının dostluk komplekslerini nasıl keşfedeceği merakla bekleniyor ve bu, gerçek dostluğun gücünü kutlayan bir hikaye sunuyor. 

 ## Sonraki Adımlar 

 **Unutulmuş Ada**'nın yayınlanma tarihleri henüz açıklanmadı, ancak bu proje, DreamWorks Animation için yeni bir heyecan verici bölümü simgeliyor. İzleyiciler, film hakkında daha fazla bilgi edinebilecek, görsel stil, yardımcı kadro ve Jo ve Raissa'nın unutulmaz yolculuğunu tanımlayan büyülü unsurları keşfedecek.

DreamWorks Animation has transported viewers to countless magical realms since 1998 and introduced us to many aspirational friendships, from Shrek and Donkey to Hiccup and Toothless. Now they seek to do both things in the singular  Forgotten Island , an original fantasy-comedy set in the 1990s Philippines and following the lives of two soon-to-be-loved besties, Jo (voiced by H.E.R.) and Raissa (voiced by Liza Soberano). Only this duo’s journey to a magical realm may cost them the friendship at the heart of the movie.  Of course friends and connection have long been the secret sauce for the makers of Forgotten Island , beginning with the writing-directing team of Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado. “For two decades, we have put so much of ourselves into every movie we do together,” Crawford shares. “That can be just jokes, things that make us laugh, or themes about being in the moment that we both really value in our own lives.” Crawford and Mercado have been real-life BFFs since working together as story artists on Kung Fu Panda 2 . And after recently working on two sequels, The Croods: A New Age (which Crawford helmed and Mercado was head of story on) and the Oscar-nominated Puss in Boots: The Last Wish (which both co-directed), the pair was eager to take on an original project. “We wanted to do something original, but really original in every sense of the word. So building a story around friendship, and our friendship, seemed the best place to start,” Crawford says.  That onscreen camaraderie also involves similarly creative spirits as personified by Jo, a livewire, and Raissa, a smartypants. They’re introduced as almost instant besties after bonding during a trip to the principal’s office in grade school. Jo even gives Raissa a friendship bracelet as a token of their newfound connection. Soon enough, they’re each other’s source of comfort, freedom, and security. In the totally tubular era of gifted mixtapes, they get close while imitating Arnold Schwarzenegger and Carl Weathers’ iconic Predator handshake at the video store, accidentally operating a retro jeepney, chronicling their canon moments through Polaroids, and adding matching charms on their bracelets. But most of all, they obsess over a tale from Jo’s grandmother (Dolly de Leon) about Nakali: a fantastical realm of monsters, spirits, and demons. Magic with Authenticity The directors drew inspiration for their heroines from the Filipino women in their own families. “For Jo and Raissa, they are heavily inspired by the strong women in our lives, especially my sister and my cousin,” Mercado says. Even their mannerisms and features would be incorporated and used in the animation. Crawford attributes Raissa’s often irked expressions to his wife, who is Filipino.
